UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT

ALEXANDRIA DIVISION
MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,
Plaintiff,
Vv. Case No. 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD
The Honorable Judge

Rossie D. Alston Jr.

KATIE HALL, individually;
NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN;
META PLATFORMS, INC;
and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,

Defendants.

PLAINTIFF’S MOTION FOR TARGETED VACATUR OF ECF NOS. 64 AND 84,
WITHDRAWAL OR MODIFICATION OF THE MAGISTRATE-JUDGE REFERRAL,
AND RELATED INTERIM RELIEF

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine moves under 28 U.S.C. § 636(b)(1)(A), 28 U.S.C. § 455,
and Federal Rules of Civil Procedure 54(b) and 72(a) for targeted vacatur of the Orders entered
September 9, 2026 (ECF No. 64) and October 7, 2026 (ECF No. 84), for withdrawal or
modification of the referral of pretrial matters to Magistrate Judge Ivan D. Davis, and for related
interim relief. A Memorandum in Support accompanies this Motion under Local Civil Rule 7(F)
(1). Plaintiff incorporates it by reference.

I. THE THREE COORDINATED APPLICATIONS

1. Plaintiff submits three applications concurrently. The Plaintiff’s Motion to Disqualify
Magistrate Judge Ivan D. Davis Under 28 U.S.C. § 455(b)(4) and § 455(a), and for Priority

Determination asks the Magistrate Judge to determine the statutory disqualification question, state

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document93_ Filed 10/13/26 Page 2 of 9 PagelD# 940

the facts on which it depends, and effect any necessary transfer of the referred matters. The
Plaintiff’s Rule 72(a) Objections to ECF No. 84 and Motion to Set Aside the Amendment and
Discovery Denials and for Coordinated Determination of the Pending Objections asks the District
Judge to correct ECF No. 84 on four procedural grounds and on a fifth ground based on the
financial-conflict evidence. This Motion asks the District Judge to determine the consequences of
that evidence for the orders already entered, to control the referral, and to protect adjudication of
the proposed Second Amended and Supplemental Complaint (ECF No. 59) and the discovery
requests (ECF Nos. 15, 54).

2. The relief requested here is cumulative of the relief requested in the Rule 72(a) objections
where both apply. It is not duplicative recovery. It is not a substitute for timely objections, and it
does not extend or restart any period to object under Rule 72(a).

II. THE EVIDENTIARY PREDICATE

3. Exhibit A to the disqualification motion is the Financial Disclosure Report (AO Form 10)
of Magistrate Judge Davis for calendar year 2025, electronically signed May 14, 2026 and May 26,
2026. Exhibit B is the Financial Disclosure Report for calendar year 2024, dated August 18, 2025.
Each report lists “FB common stock” at Part VII, line 6, with a gross year-end value of $15,001 to
$50,000. Ex. A at 2; Ex. B at 4. “FB” was the trading symbol of Facebook, Inc., which changed its
name to Meta Platforms, Inc. on October 28, 2021. Declaration of Marvelle J. Ballentine in Support
of Plaintiff’s Motion to Disqualify Magistrate Judge Ivan D. Davis 7 2—4 (“Ballentine Decl.”).

4. Meta Platforms, Inc. (“Meta”) has been a defendant since July 30, 2026. ECF Nos. 1, 5.
Meta moved to dismiss and filed its corporate disclosure statement on August 21, 2026. ECF Nos.
21, 22, 24. Magistrate Judge Davis entered ECF Nos. 62, 63, and 64 on September 9, 2026; ECF
No. 65 on September 10, 2026; ECF No. 82 on September 22, 2026; and ECF No. 84 on October 7,

2026. ECF No. 84 decides discovery directed to Meta. ECF No. 84 at 1.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document93_ Filed 10/13/26 Page 3 of 9 PagelD# 941

5. The reports establish the reported holding at year-end 2024 and year-end 2025. Plaintiff
advances continued qualifying ownership during the participation described in paragraph 4 as an
inference from the reports. Plaintiff does not allege an unreported sale, does not allege ownership
by the Magistrate Judge personally rather than by another holder covered by § 455(b)(4), and does
not allege knowledge on any particular date. The questions requiring resolution are: whether the
reported interest is a covered financial interest; the arrangement through which it is held and
whether 28 U.S.C. § 455(d)(4)(i) applies; the dates of ownership; knowledge, where § 455(b)(4)
requires it; and whether the conditions of 28 U.S.C. § 455(f) are satisfied.

6. Plaintiff was unaware of the reported financial interest when ECF No. 84 was entered
and at every earlier point in this action, and promptly presented the issue after learning of it.
Ballentine Decl. { 2.

Tl. THE ORDERS TARGETED AND THEIR CONTINUING EFFECTS

7. ECF No. 64 found that the Court “does not possess sufficient information to issue an
Order on this matter” and directed Plaintiff to provide “a redlined version of the Amended
Complaint [Dkt. Nos. 59-1, 60-1], no later than September 11, 2026,” that “must clearly indicate
the changes, deletions, and additions that were made to Plaintiff’s Complaint [Dkt. No. 1].” ECF
No. 64. Plaintiff’s objections to that order, submitted September 13, 2026, remain pending. ECF
Nos. 66, 67, 68.

8. ECF No. 84 denied ECF Nos. 15 and 54 “as premature,” stating that “the Court cannot
issue an order concerning Plaintiff’s Motions because discovery has not officially begun in this
case.” ECF No. 84 at 1. It denied ECF No. 59 on the ground that Plaintiff “was given ample
opportunity to comply with the Court’s September 9, 2026 Order [Dkt. No. 64] by producing a

redlined Second Amended Complaint but has failed to do so as of the date of this Order.” Id. at 2.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document93_ Filed 10/13/26 Page 4 of 9 PagelD# 942

9. Both orders are targeted because ECF No. 64 supplies the condition that ECF No. 84
enforced. Vacatur of the denial in ECF No. 84 while the comparison requirement and the expired
September 11 deadline in ECF No. 64 remained controlling would restore ECF No. 59 to a posture
in which the same nonproduction could produce the same denial. The relief requested as to each
order is severable.

IV. RELIEF REQUESTED

10. Plaintiff requests an order, in the form of the accompanying Proposed Order:

(R1) Referral. Withdrawing or modifying the referral of pretrial matters to Magistrate
Judge Davis, with the affected matters retained by the District Judge or reassigned through the
Court’s assignment procedures;

(R2) Vacatur. Vacating ECF No. 84 in full and vacating the comparison requirement and
the September 11, 2026 deadline in ECF No. 64, upon the statutory findings identified in paragraph
5 and the remedial findings described in the Memorandum in Support, with the relief as to each
order determined severably and matched to the period for which disqualification is established;

(R3) Restoration and preservation. Restoring ECF Nos. 15, 54, and 59 to pending status,
with every authorized submission of every party preserved, including the briefing accepted by ECF
No. 82 (ECF Nos. 78, 78-1), NCMEC and Hall’s opposition (ECF No. 74), and Meta’s opposition
(ECF No. 83);

(R4) Affirmative adjudication. Following vacatur, determining in coordination with the
Rule 72(a) objections the pending request that the District Judge grant ECF No. 59 under Rules
15(a)(2) and 15(d) and deem ECF No. 59-1 the operative pleading, and grant ECF Nos. 15 and 54
under Rule 26(d)(1), on their independently briefed merits; or alternatively, directing prompt
independent determination of the restored motions by the District Judge or a reassigned Magistrate

Judge;

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document93_ Filed 10/13/26 Page 5 of 9 PagelD# 943

(R5) Interim protection. Entering the accompanying Proposed Interim Order, which (a)
suspends further substantive action under the challenged referral pending determination of the
disqualification motion and any necessary administrative transfer; (b) suspends further reliance on
the nonproduction condition in ECF No. 64 pending determination of ECF Nos. 66 and 67, the
Rule 72(a) objections to ECF No. 84, and this Motion; and (c) directs that the amendment and
financial-conflict issues be determined before, or expressly within, any disposition of ECF Nos. 10,
21, or 45 that would terminate a claim and that relies on the exclusion of the proposed pleading.
Plaintiff does not contend that the filing of this Motion itself stays any order;

(R6) Existing objections. Determining this Motion in coordination with ECF Nos. 66, 67,
and 76 and with the Rule 72(a) objections to ECF No. 84, and identifying in the order which issues
are decided, which remain pending, and which are moot because complete relief has been granted.
The pendency of this Motion does not prevent the District Judge from granting independently
warranted relief on the Rule 72(a) objections, and Plaintiff requests that relief without awaiting
resolution of every financial-conflict question; and

(R7) Decision record. Stating findings and reasons sufficient to identify the applicable
disqualification ground, the period for which it is established, any applicable exception, and the
disposition of the retrospective relief requested.

V. POSITIONS PRESERVED
11. Plaintiff maintains that the First Amended Complaint (ECF No. 5) independently states

each of its six claims; that ECF No. 59 should be granted on its merits; and that ECF Nos. 15 and 54
are supported on the First Amended Complaint and the existing record. Nothing in this Motion
revives ECF No. 26, which remains withdrawn (ECF No. 62). Nothing in this Motion makes the
hearing or certification provisions of ECF Nos. 63, 65, or 82 a prerequisite to the relief requested,

and nothing in it withdraws the objections to those provisions in ECF Nos. 66 and 67.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document93_ Filed 10/13/26 Page 6 of 9 PagelD# 944

12. This Motion alleges no bias, hostility, improper motive, concealment, or investment-
driven decision-making. It rests on two signed financial disclosure reports, the docket, and the
statute.

VI. SUPPORTING RECORD AND SUBMISSION

13. Plaintiff submits with this Motion: the Memorandum in Support; a Proposed Interim
Order; a Proposed Order; and a Notice of Waiver of Oral Argument. This Motion relies on the
Declaration of Marvelle J. Ballentine in Support of Plaintiff’s Motion to Disqualify Magistrate
Judge Ivan D. Davis and its Exhibits A and B, submitted concurrently with the disqualification
motion and not yet assigned docket numbers, and on the existing record, including ECF Nos. 68-1,
59-2, and 31. Plaintiff submits no additional declaration.

14. Plaintiff waives oral argument on this Motion under Local Civil Rule 7(J) and requests
determination on the papers under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 78(b), or such hearing
arrangement as the Court directs. A Notice of Waiver of Oral Argument accompanies this Motion.

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff respectfully requests that the Court enter the Proposed Interim
Order and, upon determination of this Motion, the Proposed Order, granting the relief stated in

paragraph 10.

Date: October 13, 2026 Respectfully submitted,

—rD

Marvelle J. Ballentine

Plaintiff, pro se
